glance: Stocks fell about 2% (Dow -1,100) as Anthropic's debut triggered an AI selloff; VIX highest since March.
Anthropic closed its first day at $97.17, up 17% from its $83 IPO price after opening at $111.50.
After the bell, Intuit beat estimates and agreed to sell Mailchimp for $3.68 billion; shares fell.
Reuters: Meta's Muse AI agent has mixed up users' conversations and exposed private data.
Trump heads home from the Xi-Putin summit with a nuclear-risk statement but nothing on Ukraine.

tech.headline: Anthropic closes first day at $97.17, up 17% from IPO price
tech.summary: Anthropic's shares opened at $111.50, about 34% above the $83 IPO price, hit nearly $115, then faded through the afternoon to close at $97.17. The roughly $81 billion offering is the largest on record and values the company well above $1 trillion. The debut drew money out of other AI stocks, contributing to a broad market selloff, and shares slipped further after hours.

tech.headline: Intuit beats estimates and agrees to sell Mailchimp for $3.68B
tech.summary: Intuit reported first-quarter revenue up 12% and beat Wall Street estimates after the close, and said it will sell email-marketing unit Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for about $3.68 billion, far below the roughly $12 billion it paid in 2021. Shares fell sharply in after-hours trading.

tech.headline: Report: Meta's Muse agent mixed up users' conversations and data
tech.summary: Meta employees have flagged that the Muse AI agent surfaced other people's information, such as bank balances and order details, inside unrelated chats, according to internal posts reviewed by Reuters. One staffer said it prompted a reply to a Signal message without permission. Muse launched in September and has more than 10 million downloads; Meta did not immediately comment.

tech.headline: Nvidia's interim chief moves to steady staff after record quarter
tech.summary: Days after Jensen Huang's exit, interim CEO Colette Kress held Nvidia's first all-hands without him and signaled raises and equity grants would come earlier than planned, Wired reports. The company just posted $115.8 billion in quarterly revenue and guided to about $130 billion next quarter, but shares fell 3.3% Thursday in the AI selloff while the board searches for a permanent CEO.

tech.headline: AI-discovered NGINX flaw lets attackers take over servers
tech.summary: Security firm Xint used AI models to uncover five flaws in NGINX, one of the web's most widely used server programs, including an unauthenticated remote-code-execution bug dating to 2015 that works on default settings. F5, which maintains NGINX, began issuing patches Wednesday and urged immediate updates; Wiz says it found the same flaws independently. Researchers estimate millions of exposed servers could be vulnerable.

tech.headline: Palo Alto Networks buys AI startup Applied Compute for $4.5B
tech.summary: Palo Alto Networks agreed to acquire Applied Compute in an all-stock deal worth about $4.5 billion, extending its push into AI-driven security. It also reported revenue up 39% to $3.44 billion and raised its full-year outlook; shares rose about 6.4% Thursday, bucking the market slide.

tech.headline: Google rolls out Gemini 4 Neon
tech.summary: Google released Gemini 4 Neon, a middle tier between its top Carbon and fast Hydrogen models, across the Gemini API, Antigravity and the Gemini app for paid users, claiming top marks on a coding-agent index at $3 per million input tokens. Google also renamed its Gemini Spark agent to Tasks and made it free in six countries, and opened Genie 4 world-generation to AI Ultra subscribers.

other.headline: Wall Street's worst day in months as AI stocks slide
other.summary: The Dow lost about 1,100 points and the S&P 500 and Nasdaq each fell more than 2% after an early rally collapsed once Anthropic began trading. Investors sold Nvidia, Amazon, Alphabet and other AI winners, and the VIX fear gauge hit its highest level since March.

other.headline: Trump heads home after three-way summit with Xi and Putin
other.summary: The rare Trump-Xi-Putin meeting in China produced a joint statement on nuclear risk and UN reform but little concrete progress and no mention of Ukraine. Analysts described the summit as heavy on symbolism, with the leaders' warm rhetoric outpacing actual agreements.

other.headline: Jobless claims tick up; Fed hike talk lingers
other.summary: Initial unemployment claims rose by 1,000 to 203,000, slightly above forecasts but still low. With inflation running hot, futures traders are pricing quarter-point Fed rate hikes in December and January, and the 10-year Treasury yield is holding above 5%.

other.headline: Officials: recent outages were not a coordinated attack
other.summary: At a House Homeland Security hearing, DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin, DNI Jay Clayton and the FBI said a run of outages, including an FAA ground stop, bank and Microsoft service failures, and an NSA network outage, stemmed from separate maintenance and technical changes. The FBI said it found no sign of malicious cyber activity.

other.headline: Jeffries nominated for Speaker; Peltola wins Alaska Senate race
other.summary: House Democrats easily nominated Hakeem Jeffries for Speaker, putting him in line to become the first Black Speaker when the new Congress convenes. In Alaska, Democrat Mary Peltola was projected to win the Senate race.

markets.summary: Stocks reversed early gains and fell about 2% as Anthropic's debut sparked profit-taking in AI names; the VIX jumped to about 28, its highest since March.
